title: Recycled vs. New Auto Parts: Where Can You Save?
md:
If your repair estimate calls for a new factory part, ask your shop to price a recycled OEM part too. A used factory mirror, door, or tail light can cost less than its new counterpart. And depending on what’s included, a recycled assembly can sometimes save you money elsewhere on the estimate.

The savings come down to the part you need, the condition it’s in, and what your shop has to do to install it. Here’s how to compare your options before you approve the repair.

What is a recycled OEM auto part?

OEM stands for original equipment manufacturer. A recycled OEM part is a factory part removed from another vehicle for reuse. You’re buying a used version of the original part, so you can compare it directly with a new factory replacement once you’ve confirmed it fits your vehicle.

If your estimate includes a new aftermarket part, compare that option too. New factory and new aftermarket parts can come at different prices, so check which one your shop quoted before you compare it with a recycled part.

Which recycled auto parts are worth pricing first?

Mirrors and lights. The same car can come with several versions of a side mirror or headlight. A mirror might have heat, power folding, or a blind spot indicator. A headlight might use a different connector or require a separate module. Ask what’s included in each quote so you can compare the same features and see whether you’ll need to buy anything separately.

Doors, fenders, and liftgates. A recycled panel in the right color and condition may save on paint work. Ask your shop to check the paint match and what comes with the panel. A door shell and a door assembly can mean different amounts of work, especially if the shop needs to transfer glass, wiring, or hardware.

Engines and transmissions. A lower part price can make a difference on a major repair, but installation is a big part of the decision. Compare the used unit’s mileage, condition, and warranty with the other options your shop quotes. Ask what the warranty covers if the part needs to be replaced and whether labor coverage is available. B&R warranty FAQs

Compare the installed cost of recycled and new parts

Ask your shop to quote both options for the same repair. Then check what each estimate includes:

Part and delivery. Include shipping or pickup costs and ask about any refundable core deposit.

Installation and supplies. Check whether labor, fluids, seals, or other items needed for the job are included.

Paint, programming, or calibration. Ask what the part needs before it’s ready to use on your vehicle.

Warranty coverage. Confirm what’s covered and whether you’d pay for labor again if the part had to come out.

If you’re buying the part yourself, check with your shop first. Ask whether they’ll install a customer supplied part and how that affects their labor warranty. Have your VIN and the part number from your estimate handy when you shop so you can confirm the fit before ordering.

Check B&R before you buy new

Already have a repair estimate? Use it to look up a recycled option. Compare the part price, confirm what’s included, and ask your shop what it would cost to install. That will show you what you could save on the repair as a whole. [Search recycled auto parts at B&R](https://www.autowrecking.com)

title: Quality Recycled Engines and Transmissions: A Smarter Way to Keep Vehicles on the Road
md:
When an engine or transmission fails, replacing the entire vehicle isn’t always the best option. At B&R, we help repair shops and vehicle owners find quality recycled engines, transmissions, and other automotive components at a fraction of the cost of buying new.

With an extensive inventory of recycled OEM parts across our network of locations, B&R provides practical, affordable solutions that help keep vehicles running and repair costs manageable.

Why Choose Recycled Engines and Transmissions?

Replacing an engine or transmission can be one of the most expensive repairs a vehicle owner faces. Purchasing a brand-new component isn’t always necessary, especially when a quality recycled replacement is available.

Recycled engines and transmissions offer several advantages:

* Significant Cost Savings: Recycled components typically cost considerably less than new OEM replacements, making major repairs more affordable.
* Original Equipment Fit: OEM components are manufactured to meet the original vehicle specifications, helping ensure proper fit and compatibility.
* Environmental Benefits: Reusing existing automotive components reduces waste and helps conserve the materials and energy required to manufacture new parts.
* Availability: Recycled parts can provide an alternative when new components are expensive, backordered, or no longer manufactured.

For many vehicles, a recycled engine or transmission offers an economical way to extend the vehicle’s useful life.

An Extensive Inventory of Automotive Components

At B&R, inventory is one of our greatest strengths.

Our facilities house a wide variety of recycled automotive components, including engines, transmissions, transfer cases, differentials, and other drivetrain parts.

With locations throughout the western United States, our network gives customers access to a broad selection of parts for domestic and imported vehicles.

Whether you’re a professional repair shop looking for a replacement engine or a vehicle owner searching for a hard-to-find transmission, our team can help identify available options.

Our inventory system helps connect customers with parts across our network, expanding the search beyond a single location.

Supporting Professional Repair Shops

We understand that automotive repair professionals need more than competitive pricing. They need dependable parts, accurate information, and a supplier that understands the importance of keeping repairs moving.

A vehicle sitting in a repair bay waiting for parts can affect shop productivity, customer satisfaction, and scheduling.

That’s why B&R works with collision repair facilities, mechanical repair shops, dealerships, and other automotive businesses to help source the components they need.

Our team can assist with identifying compatible parts, checking availability, and coordinating orders.

From individual engine replacements to ongoing parts sourcing, our goal is to make recycled automotive parts a convenient option for professional repair facilities.

Giving Automotive Parts a Second Life

Every recycled engine or transmission represents an opportunity to make better use of an existing resource.

When a vehicle reaches the end of its useful life, many of its mechanical components may still have years of service remaining.

Rather than allowing those components to go to waste, automotive recycling makes it possible to recover and reuse valuable parts.

This process helps reduce the demand for newly manufactured components while providing customers with affordable replacement options.

It’s a practical example of how automotive recycling benefits both vehicle owners and the environment.

Finding the Right Engine or Transmission

Not every engine or transmission is interchangeable, even between vehicles of the same make and model.

Factors such as model year, engine configuration, drivetrain, transmission type, and specific vehicle options can affect compatibility.

When searching for a replacement, having the vehicle identification number (VIN) available can help narrow down the correct options.

Our experienced parts professionals can help customers navigate these details and locate suitable replacement components.

Providing accurate vehicle information from the beginning can help simplify the process and reduce the possibility of ordering an incompatible part.

Your First Call for Quality Recycled Auto Parts

At B&R, we’re committed to helping customers find affordable solutions for their automotive repair needs.

From engines and transmissions to thousands of other recycled OEM components, our extensive inventory and knowledgeable team make us a valuable resource for repair professionals and vehicle owners alike.
